channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Euro-area consumer prices rose 3.8% year on year in September, according to an initial estimate, up from 3.2% in August and the highest rate since September 2023, driven by high energy prices, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports, citing Eurostat.
item.description:
The rate is well above the ECB's medium-term target of 2%, and economists therefore expect the ECB to raise its key rates for the third time this year, taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, according to the report. The reporting does not give core inflation, the energy component, or rates by member state, and does not name the date of the ECB's next decision.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The inflation rate is an initial estimate; the rate rise is an expectation of economists, not a decision. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, energy-driven inflation raises input and wage pressure across manufacturing, and higher policy rates weigh on interest-sensitive demand, first of all construction and durable goods. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, both effects reach the business at once: costs through energy and wages, and demand through construction and vehicle purchases financed with credit. Points that may be worth considering include the core rate, which shows whether energy is passing through to other prices, and how pricing in customer contracts tracks inflation.

Süddeutsche Zeitung

item.title: China's Ministry of Commerce opened an anti-dumping investigation on 3 October into imports of the chemical p-nitrotoluene from the EU, to be completed by 3 October 2027 and extendable by six months in exceptional circumstances.
item.description:
The investigation was requested on 14 September by Jiangsu Huaihe Chemical and Hubei Oriental Chemical on behalf of China's p-nitrotoluene industry, Lianhe Zaobao reports. According to the ministry spokesperson cited by Bjd.com.cn, the applicant's preliminary evidence points to high import volumes from Europe between 2022 and 2025 and a cumulative price decline of almost 60%, which the applicant says damaged China's domestic industry. Commercial Times reports the step ahead of EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič's visit to China on 8–9 October for talks with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao; Arab News reports that he heads to Beijing for two days of meetings to try to stave off a trade war, while the EU develops new trade defence tools that China has threatened to retaliate against. The News International notes that the EU has imposed measures to slow the inflow of fast fashion and electric vehicles from China. The reporting does not give the volume or value of EU exports concerned, the EU producers named, or a response from the Commission.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The investigation is opened, not concluded; no duty has been set. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, p-nitrotoluene is an intermediate used in dyes, pigments and agrochemicals, so the direct trade at stake is likely small, and the timing places the case within the wider EU–China trade dispute. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, a chemical intermediate becoming a subject of trade defence signals that EU chemical exports to China can be drawn into the dispute, which reaches supply chains that cross the two markets. Points that may be worth considering include whether further Chinese investigations into EU chemicals follow the 8–9 October talks, and how the Commission responds.

Lianhe Zaobao | Bjd.com.cn | Commercial Times | Arab News | The News International

item.title: US construction employment rose by 11,000 in September, and AGC says the gains brought the industry's unemployment rate down to 3.5%, with nonresidential firms adding 16,100 jobs while residential builders and subcontractors lost 4,900.
item.description:
Over 12 months nonresidential construction firms added 142,000 jobs, or 2.9%, while residential employment fell by 32,800, or 1.0%, according to the Associated General Contractors of America. Nonresidential specialty trade contractors added 12,300 employees in September and heavy and civil engineering construction 2,600. Across the US economy, 29,000 jobs were added in September and the unemployment rate stood at 4.2%, with manufacturing adding 9,000 jobs, Anadolu Agency reports, citing the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The reporting does not give hours worked, wage growth in construction, a breakdown of nonresidential growth by project type, or the industry's previous unemployment rate.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Employment is a measure of activity but not of volume put in place, and the figures split clearly between nonresidential growth and residential decline. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, nonresidential employment growth in the US has been associated with data-centre and infrastructure work, and residential weakness with high mortgage rates. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the split matters because residential and nonresidential building use different mixes of sealants, flooring adhesives and construction chemicals. Points that may be worth considering include whether residential employment stabilises as rates move, and which nonresidential segments carry the growth.

Associated General Contractors of America | Anadolu Agency

item.title: GM, Ford and Stellantis accounted for around 37% of the US new-car market in the third quarter, about as little as in summer 2021, Handelsblatt reports, while Cox Automotive projects Asian brands above 50% for a second quarter.
item.description:
Handelsblatt says the decline is not yet definitively confirmed because data from other competitors are missing, and names as one reason a shift away from large combustion SUVs as petrol averaged around USD 4.47 a gallon, with buyers increasingly turning to hybrids. Cox Automotive senior economist Charlie Chesbrough, quoted by Japan Today, projects the Detroit three's share at a bit over 36%, the lowest on record. In the third quarter GM's sales fell 5.5% to 670,974 units while Toyota's rose 0.6% to 633,223, and over nine months GM's share fell to 16.7% from 17.4% while Toyota's rose to 15.6% from 15.2%, according to Japan Today. The reporting does not give total US third-quarter sales or the hybrid share.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The share figures are early and differ between sources — around 37% and a bit over 36% — and both are shares, not volumes. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a share shift between brands changes which suppliers and assembly plants carry the volume more than the total material needed, and a move from large SUVs to hybrids changes vehicle size and drivetrain mix. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the relevant question is which assembly plants gain volume and how hybrid drivetrains change bonding and sealing content per vehicle. Points that may be worth considering include confirmed third-quarter totals, and whether fuel prices keep driving the mix shift.

Handelsblatt | Japan Today

item.title: South Korea's exports rose 83.5% year on year in September to USD 120.94 billion and semiconductor exports rose 262.8% to USD 60.3 billion, Commercial Times reports, citing the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.
item.description:
Imports rose 26% to USD 71.09 billion, according to the report. Semiconductors thus made up about half of September exports by value. In Taiwan, Micron, the largest foreign investor there, has invested TWD 1.6 trillion over the past four years to expand four bases focused on high-bandwidth memory, an investment that Yahoo! Taiwan says exceeds the total of the past 25 years, and Powerchip, Winbond and Nanya Technology are also expanding, the report says, citing a supply shortage in the memory market. The reporting does not give export volumes as opposed to values, the reason for the rise, or exports by destination.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The export figures are values in US dollars, so they combine price and volume, and the reporting does not separate the two. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a memory shortage such as the one cited in the Taiwan report would tend to lift prices, and a surge of this size in chip export values reflects investment in AI data-centre hardware, with capacity additions in memory and packaging following at a lag. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, semiconductor packaging and electronics assembly use specialised bonding, encapsulation and thermal materials, so growth in memory output can raise demand in that segment. Points that may be worth considering include how much of the growth is volume, and where new packaging capacity is being built.

Commercial Times | Yahoo! Taiwan

item.title: US production of major plastic resins rose 1.7% in August from July to 9.1 billion pounds, 0.7% below August 2025, while sales and captive use rose 3.8% from a year earlier, the American Chemistry Council reports.
item.description:
Year-to-date production rose 4.3% to 71.3 billion pounds, according to the American Chemistry Council. Sales and captive use also rose 1.7% month on month to 9.1 billion pounds, and year-to-date sales and captive use rose 2.2% to 69.8 billion pounds. The reporting does not break the figures down by resin type, end market or export share, or give prices. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The figures are measured production and sales volumes; in August, sales and captive use rose 3.8% year on year while production fell 0.7%, but year to date production grew faster (4.3% against 2.2%), and in August both stood at 9.1 billion pounds. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, US resin output is closely tied to ethane-based feedstock that has been less exposed to the Middle East supply disruption than naphtha-based production. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, resins and polymers are core raw materials, and US volumes indicate availability in the North American supply base. Points that may be worth considering include how US resin availability and prices compare with Europe and Asia, and which product lines rely on US-sourced polymers.

American Chemistry Council

item.title: At least 16.5 million barrels a day of crude left the Gulf region excluding Iran between 1 and 28 September, matching the pre-war average, with 40% exported through Saudi and UAE pipelines that avoid the Strait of Hormuz, Kpler data show.
item.description:
Before the war 83% of the region's crude crossed the Strait of Hormuz, The Times of India reports; of the 60% that crossed it in September, most moved on shuttle tankers, Kpler's Emmanuel Belostrino said. Separate preliminary Kpler data cited by Lianhe Zaobao, covering the wider Middle East including the Red Sea and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, put the seven-day average of crude exports at 18.5 million barrels a day as of 1 October, against a pre-war average of 18 million. BBC News, also citing Kpler, reports that daily oil flow from the Middle East reached 92% of its pre-war baseline in the final week of September, and that Iran's oil exports have ground to a halt since the US reimposed a naval blockade in July. OPEC+ core members kept November production targets steady on 4 October; in August they pumped 25 million barrels a day, still roughly 5 million below pre-war levels in February, MarketScreener reports, citing OPEC data. Les Echos reports that markets remain under tension and prices high. The reporting does not give refined-product flows from the Gulf, or freight and insurance costs on the bypass routes.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The Kpler figures are export flows with different scopes and are not combined here; OPEC+ production is a different measure and remains below pre-war levels. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, crude supply recovering through bypass routes reduces physical shortage risk, while prices stay high because the routes depend on pipelines and shuttle tankers that remain exposed to attack. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, crude availability feeds petrochemical raw materials, but refined products and their prices are the more direct link. Points that may be worth considering include whether product flows recover as crude has, and how sensitive the bypass routes are to further attacks.

The Times of India | Lianhe Zaobao | BBC News | MarketScreener | Les Echos

item.title: Toyota Motor Thailand and Honda Automobile (Thailand) have temporarily suspended vehicle production at all their assembly plants in Thailand because flooding prevents suppliers from delivering parts, The Nation reports.
item.description:
Toyota has suspended its three main assembly plants — Samrong in Samut Prakan, and Ban Pho and Gateway in Chachoengsao — and a plant operated by its affiliate Toyota Auto Works, after more than 320 millimetres of rain in three days left major transport routes flooded, according to The Nation; suppliers could not deliver components to Toyota's just-in-time production system as scheduled, causing parts shortages. Thailand's Industry Ministry estimates direct flood damage at THB 147.84 million across 4,216 businesses in 55 provinces as of 2 October, most of them small and medium-sized, The Nation reports, and the Finance Ministry says the floods' impact on the overall economy is under 0.1% and keeps its growth forecast for this year at 2% to 2.5%, Lianhe Zaobao reports. A Rangsit University economist estimates that the flooding could reduce third-quarter growth by about 0.5 percentage point, The Nation reports. In an earlier report, Taiwanese electronics makers including Delta Electronics said production at their Thai plants was generally normal, with effects concentrated on road traffic, logistics and staff attendance, Commercial Times reports. The reporting does not say how long the suspensions will last, how many vehicles are affected, or which suppliers are flooded.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The suspensions are temporary and their duration is not reported; the economic estimates come from different bodies with different scopes and are not combined here. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, Thailand is a large regional base for vehicle assembly and export, and a just-in-time halt at carmakers passes back through their component suppliers. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, bonding and sealing volumes at Thai assembly and supplier plants fall while lines are stopped, and a restart can bring catch-up demand. Points that may be worth considering include when production restarts, and whether other carmakers or electronics plants in Thailand report similar halts.

The Nation - Thailand | The Nation - Thailand | Lianhe Zaobao | The Nation - Thailand | Commercial Times

item.title: A VDMA flash survey of more than 400 member companies finds that two out of three machinery manufacturers face competition from products that do not meet fundamental legal safety requirements, and over half have lost contracts to such suppliers.
item.description:
Many of these products originate from China, but also from other countries, according to VDMA. The association says over 50% of companies have lost contracts to suppliers that obtain price advantages from lower safety standards. It demands that manufacturers from third countries have a mandatory and validated EU representative with clearly defined responsibilities, and Handelsblatt reports that it wants manufacturers of unsafe machines put on a blacklist that must immediately lead to an import ban, as the US and India already do. Handelsblatt describes the demand as stricter market surveillance of imports from third countries by Germany's mechanical engineering sector. The reporting does not give the value of contracts lost, the machine categories most affected, or a response from the Commission or the German government.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The shares come from a survey of members; the blacklist and import bans are the association's demands, not measures. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, price competition from lower-cost machinery puts pressure on European machine builders' volumes and margins, and stricter market surveillance would raise compliance requirements for imported equipment. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, German machinery makers are industrial customers for bonding and sealing, and their order situation reaches demand in general industry. Points that may be worth considering include whether the EU takes up mandatory representation for third-country manufacturers, and whether similar surveillance demands extend to other product categories, including components and materials.

VDMA | Handelsblatt | Yahoo! Germany

item.title: New-car registrations in September rose 12.1% year on year in the UK to 350,518, according to preliminary SMMT data, car sales in Spain rose 10% to 93,858, the best September in 20 years, and Italian registrations rose 9.9% to 139,356.
item.description:
In the UK, battery-electric registrations rose 36.3% to 99,199, a 28.3% share; over nine months electric cars were 26.2% of sales, below the 33% mandated for 2026, MarketScreener reports, citing SMMT figures. SMMT says it was the UK's highest ever monthly battery-electric volume, and the best September overall since 2017, with growth largely driven by intense competition, particularly from new entrants, increased choice and attractive deals. In Spain, electrified vehicles (pure electric and plug-in hybrids) were 34% of September sales, and the Tesla Model 3 was the best-selling model, the first time an electric car has topped monthly sales, La Vanguardia reports. In Italy, nine-month registrations rose 8.7% to 1,268,964 but remain 13.6% below 2019; in September, hybrids took 50.7% and diesel fell to 4.9%, Il Sole 24 Ore reports. By contrast, car sales in Turkey fell 27.8% year on year to 63,736, Dünya reports, citing the distributors' association ODMD. The reporting does not give German or French September figures, or production volumes in these countries.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

These are registration and sales figures, preliminary in the UK's case, and they record demand, not production; SMMT attributes the UK rise to competition and deals, and Italy's nine-month total remains below 2019. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a market growing through new entrants and imports can raise sales without raising European assembly volumes, and a fast shift to electrified drivetrains changes which components are bonded, sealed and thermally managed. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the mix shift toward battery-electric and hybrid vehicles matters as much as the volume. Points that may be worth considering include how much of the growth is supplied from European plants, and whether German and French September data show the same pattern.

MarketScreener | SMMT | La Vanguardia | Il Sole 24 Ore | ANSA | Dünya Gazetesi

item.title: The G7, coordinated by the IEA, will release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves over four months, starting immediately, with a substantial diesel release front-loaded into the first 20 days.
item.description:
The release was announced on 2 October, the Los Angeles Times and China Economic Net report, in a G7 leaders' statement issued by the office of French President Emmanuel Macron, who chairs the G7, according to Nikkei Asian Review; The Guardian gives the volume as up to 100 million barrels. The G7 agreed after pressure from President Trump and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions, The Standard reports. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had called on Europeans to release their strategic diesel reserves "promptly", a demand Trump supported, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports, and the EU strongly opposed a US threat to ban diesel exports, Yahoo! Taiwan reports. The IEA says member countries have released 325 million of the 400 million barrels pledged in March; the G7 did not say whether the new 100 million barrels includes the outstanding 75 million or comes on top, The Straits Times reports. The US national average diesel price was USD 6.37 a gallon on 2 October after a record USD 6.52 on 22 September, the Los Angeles Times reports, citing AAA. Brent fell 0.34% to USD 101.90 a barrel by 01:15 GMT on 5 October, The Standard reports. The reporting does not give the split between diesel and crude, or each country's share.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The volume and schedule are stated, but whether they are additional to the March pledge is not, so the net addition to supply cannot be read from the reporting. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a front-loaded diesel release targets the product whose shortage has driven prices hardest, and the pledge against energy export restrictions, reported by The Standard, would reduce the risk of transatlantic supply being diverted. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the diesel part of the release reaches logistics and freight costs directly, while the crude part, whose size is not given, is closer to petrochemical raw materials. Points that may be worth considering include whether diesel prices in Europe respond within the 20-day window, and how freight surcharges in supply contracts follow.

Business Standard | Nikkei Asian Review | The Guardian | Los Angeles Times | China Economic Net | The Straits Times | The Standard | Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | Yahoo! Taiwan

item.title: The Ifo business climate for Germany's chemical industry rose to +5.5 points in September from -2.6 in August, its second consecutive monthly improvement, with expectations up to +2.3 from -15.0.
item.description:
Companies again assessed their current business situation positively, at +8.8 points, Handelsblatt reports. Ifo says the recovery is driven by exports and orders from manufacturing, and that higher government spending on defence and infrastructure supports the industry through intermediate purchases; according to Ifo industry expert Anna Wolf, customers at home and abroad continue to replenish their inventories and accept higher prices. The order backlog is still considered very low, and with high costs the earnings situation remains strained. Handelsblatt also attributes the improvement partly to rising foreign demand. MarketScreener reports that the index entered positive territory for the first time this year and that demand support from Middle East supply disruptions bolstered the sector. Handelsblatt describes chemicals as Germany's third-largest industrial sector, after automotive and mechanical engineering. The reporting does not give production or capacity-utilisation figures, the share of the improvement coming from price rather than volume, or a breakdown by chemical segment.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The index measures sentiment, not output, and Ifo itself mentions restocking and customers accepting higher prices alongside exports and manufacturing orders, with backlogs considered very low. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, improvements that rest partly on restocking can fade once inventories are rebuilt, so a sentiment turn is a weaker signal than a rise in orders. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, an improving domestic chemical industry can mean steadier raw-material supply from German producers, while acceptance of higher prices along the chain points to continued pressure on input costs. Points that may be worth considering include whether production data in the coming months confirm the sentiment turn, and how much of current customer demand reflects restocking rather than end use.

Handelsblatt | Handelsblatt | MarketScreener
